questions.question_text: Find the exact length of the projection of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 12 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Used the signed value $\frac{-8}{13}$ without taking its absolute value; a length cannot be negative.
Divided the absolute dot product by $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 169$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 13$.
Ignored the negative first component of $\underset{\sim}{a}$, using $(4)(5)+(1)(12) = 32$ for the dot product.
Ignored the direction of $\underset{\sim}{b}$; the projection must be a multiple of $-2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and the scalar $\frac{5}{2}$ is positive.
Projected onto the $x$-direction instead of onto $\underset{\sim}{b}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 2$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 4$.

questions.question_text:
$|\overrightarrow{OA}| = 18$ and $\angle AOB = 30^{\circ}$.
Find the exact length of the projection of $\overrightarrow{OA}$ onto $\overrightarrow{OB}$.

options.why: Used $18\sin 30^{\circ}$ instead of $18\cos 30^{\circ}$, finding the perpendicular component's length.
Used $\sqrt{3}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $\cos 30^{\circ}$.
Divided by $\cos 30^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying, obtaining $\frac{18}{\sqrt{3}/2} = 12\sqrt{3}$, then incorrectly halved that result.

questions.question_text:
The points $A(0,1)$ and $B(8,7)$ are given.
Find the projection of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{c} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Used $\overrightarrow{BA} = \begin{pmatrix} -8 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$ instead of $\overrightarrow{AB}$, reversing the sign of the dot product.
Projected $\underset{\sim}{c}$ onto $\overrightarrow{AB}$ instead of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{c}$.
Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{c}| = \sqrt{5}$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{c}|^{2} = 5$.
Projected $\underset{\sim}{b}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{a}$, using $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2} = 170$ and multiplying by $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
Divided the dot product $-17$ by $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 17$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 289$.
Used $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2} = 170$ in the denominator while still multiplying by $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

questions.question_text:
The projection of $m\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}$ onto $5\underset{\sim}{i}+12\underset{\sim}{j}$ has length $\dfrac{9}{13}$.
Find all possible values of $m$.

options.why: Solved only $5m-36 = 9$ and ignored the second case $5m-36 = -9$ of the absolute value.
Set $5m-36$ equal to $\pm 9$ but then solved as if the $36$ were also negative.
After obtaining $5m = 45$ or $5m = 27$, divided by the vector's magnitude $13$ instead of the coefficient $5$.

questions.question_text: Find the projection of $\underset{\sim}{a} = -2\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$ in the direction of $\underset{\sim}{b} = 4\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$.

options.why: Divided by $|\underset{\sim}{b}| = 5$ instead of $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2} = 25$.
Projected $\underset{\sim}{b}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{a}$, dividing by $|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2} = 40$ and multiplying by $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
Multiplied the scalar $\frac{2}{5}$ by $\underset{\sim}{a}$ instead of by $\underset{\sim}{b}$.
